newsitem.title: INDONESIA: ASEAN officials prepare for ministers' meeting.
newsitem.headline: ASEAN officials prepare for ministers' meeting.

text.p: Senior officials from seven Southeast Asian nations started a two-day meeting on Monday to finalise the agenda for ASEAN economic ministers at their annual gathering this week.

The ministers of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations will review progress in reducing and eliminating tariff and non-tariff barriers at a council meeting of the ASEAN Free Trade Area (AFTA) on Wednesday.

At their annual meeting on Thursday, the ministers were expected to review reports on AFTA, services and intellectual property agreement, and the ASEAN Industrial Cooperation Agreement, officials said.
Othe topics will include the ASEAN Investment Area aimed at boosting investment within and from outside the region, and cooperation in developing the Mekong river basin.

ASEAN Secretary-General Ajit Singh said the ministers would also be looking at preparations for the 18-member Asia-Pacific Regional Cooperation (APEC) forum meeting in Manila in November and the first ministerial meeting of the World Trade Organisation (WTO) in Singapore in December.
Officials said preparations for an informal ASEAN summit in Indonesia in December would be discussed. The final date for the summit has yet to be announced.
On Friday ASEAN ministers will meet their counterparts from Australia and New Zealand as part of the Closer Economic Relations programme, and Japan's Ministry of International Trade and Industry.

ASEAN observers Cambodia and Laos will attend the meetings before they become full members of the group next year. ASEAN comprises Indonesia, Malaysia, Thailand, Singapore, Brunei, Vietnam and the Philippines.
